messages.content: "Imagine you are a drone operator. You are currently operating a drone that is at a point (5, 7) in the sky. You are asked to move the drone to a new point (10, 15). After reaching the new point, you are again asked to move the drone to another point (20, 25). Can you calculate the total distance the drone has traveled using the Euclidean norm method?"

function.name: math_hypot
function.description: Calculate the Euclidean norm, sqrt(sum(squares)), the length of the vector from the origin to point (x, y) which is the hypotenuse of the right triangle. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

z.description: Optional. The z-coordinate value. Default is 0.

First distance: dx=10-5=5, dy=15-7=8. sqrt(5^2+8^2)=sqrt(25+64)=sqrt(89). sqrt(89) ≈ 9.433... Actually sqrt(89)=9.433... Let's compute precisely: 9.433... We'll keep as sqrt(89).

Second distance: dx=20-10=10, dy=25-15=10. sqrt(10^2+10^2)=sqrt(200)=10*sqrt(2) ≈ 14.1421.

Total distance: sqrt(89)+10*sqrt(2). Approx numeric: sqrt(89)=9.433..., 10*sqrt(2)=14.1421, sum=23.575... So answer: about 23.58 units.
